newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy Btps seen positive early '97, problems later.
newsitem.headline: Italy Btps seen positive early '97, problems later.

text.p: The Italian bond (Btp) market still has room to gain at the start of the coming year but the picture is likely to change as the second quarter looms, Credito Italiano bank said in a quarterly research note.

An expected contract renewal deal between employers and metal workers' unions, a forecast 75 basis point cut in the discount rate, now 7.5 percent, and a supportive international situation would all help to support Btps in coming weeks.

Credito saw the spread of the 10-year Btp over the 10-year Bund narrowing to 160 basis points after its record low of 168 this week and today's 172 basis points close. The yield on the 10-year Btp was forecast to fall to 7.3 percent from 7.59 percent today.
But the convergence process was expected to be interrupted towards the second quarter when the direction of monetary policy in Germany and Japan may change, it said.

In addition, data about the state of Italy's finances was likely to show the country having difficulty reaching the three percent budget deficit to GDP ratio which is a criterion for joining Europe's single currency in 1999.
As a result, Credito forecast Italy would need an additional 1997 mini-budget of at least 15.0 trillion lire, on top of the 62.5 trillion lire package currently going through parliament.

In that event, some political risk was likely to resurface linked to Prime Minister Romano Prodi's need for agreement on certain measures, like early pension reforms, with the hard-left Communist Refoundation party, whose support he needs to pass legislation in the lower house of parliament.
In the light of all this, Credito forecast the 10-year Btp yield to rise to 8.0 percent in March and the spread over the Bund to widen out to 200 basis points.
But it said the scenario for 1997 remained bond-supportive on the whole with yields falling to around 7.5 percent again in June.
